text: Definition. Let t be a real number and let P = (x, y) be the point on the unit circle that corresponds to t. Then sin t = y, cos t = x and tan t = y/x for x ≠ 0. The arc length from (1, 0) to P equals t because the radius is 1.
Example 3. Find the exact values of sin t and cos t when t = 5π/6. The terminal point is in Quadrant II with reference number π/6, so sin(5π/6) = 1/2 and cos(5π/6) = −√3/2.
